builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: TERRA: Task-Oriented Edge AI for Regional Fire Detection with Identity-Free Reporting
summary: TERRA replaces per-device raw measurement transmission and device-identified reconstruction with tiny task-oriented reports (a quantized fire probability or a compact learned feature) aggregated by a permutation-invariant DeepSets model at the receiver. The cost is training and deploying per-device edge inference plus the aggregation model, and accepting evidence fusion rather than recoverable per-sensor data. It can fail under degraded uplink conditions: missed or falsely recovered messages erode accuracy, and while TERRA-Score is more robust to false-message contamination, both modes depend on report availability and were validated only on a single indoor EN54 testbed, so transfer to real outdoor fire deployments is unproven.
rationale: This is a niche distributed-sensing edge framework whose value applies only if the team builds multi-device monitoring over constrained uplinks, which falls outside typical LLM-centric production work but is inexpensive to evaluate if such a use case exists.
technique: Identity-free edge reports with DeepSets regional aggregation

claims.statement: TERRA replaces per-device raw measurement transmission and device-identified reconstruction with tiny task-oriented reports (a quantized fire probability or a compact learned feature) aggregated by a permutation-invariant DeepSets model at the receiver. The cost is training and deploying per-device edge inference plus the aggregation model, and accepting evidence fusion rather than recoverable per-sensor data. It can fail under degraded uplink conditions: missed or falsely recovered messages erode accuracy, and while TERRA-Score is more robust to false-message contamination, both modes depend on report availability and were validated only on a single indoor EN54 testbed, so transfer to real outdoor fire deployments is unproven.

With nine reports and perfect recovery, TERRA-Feature reaches mean AUPRC 0.990 with a 24-bit payload and TERRA-Score 0.987 with 6 bits, both at 1.81% missed-detection rate at FAR ≤ 1%, on the EN54 indoor fire-alarm dataset.
